lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.season: 2026 boat season: Jan–Mar closed; Apr–Jun all depths; Jul–Sep shoreward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line; Oct–Dec offshore-only for lingcod and shelf/slope rockfish. Nearshore rockfish closed Oct–Dec.

windows.restriction: Only shoreward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line; exact position must be checked.
Only seaward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line for lingcod and shelf/slope rockfish. Nearshore rockfish closed. The 200-ft preset is not an access clearance.

lingcod.bag: 2 per person daily/in possession; separate from the 10-fish RCG group but included in the general 20-finfish aggregate.
details: Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting lingcod, or when lingcod are aboard. Your double-drop rig fits that limit.
Carry a descending device ready for immediate use.
Fillets aboard: at least 14 in, with all skin attached.
Groundfish Exclusion Areas remain closed to recreational groundfish. Use official coordinates to check seasonal RCA access.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

rockfish.season: 2026 boat season: Jan–Mar closed; Apr–Jun all depths; Jul–Sep shoreward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line; Oct–Dec offshore-only for lingcod and shelf/slope rockfish. Nearshore rockfish closed Oct–Dec.

windows.restriction: Only shoreward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line; exact position must be checked.
Only seaward of the legal 50-fathom RCA line for lingcod and shelf/slope rockfish. Nearshore rockfish closed. The 200-ft preset is not an access clearance.

rockfish.bag: 10 combined rockfish/cabezon/greenlings daily/in possession, within the general 20-finfish aggregate. Within those ten: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 2 vermilion/sunset combined.
rockfish.size: No minimum length for retained rockfish. Species must be identified.
details: Within the 10: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 2 vermilion/sunset rockfish combined.
No retention of yelloweye, quillback, cowcod or bronzespotted rockfish.
Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting rockfish, or when rockfish are aboard. Carry a descending device ready for use.
Retained rockfish fillets must have all skin attached.
Groundfish Exclusion Areas remain closed to recreational groundfish. Use official coordinates to check seasonal RCA access.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. This card covers waters south of Point Sur.
halibut.bag: 5 fish daily and in possession south of Point Sur.
details: California halibut only; Pacific halibut has a different season and rules.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply. With rockfish or lingcod aboard, use one line and no more than two hooks; salmon aboard triggers salmon gear rules.
Fillets aboard: at least 16¾ in with all skin attached. Do not gaff an undersized fish.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.season: 2026 fall season: Sep 1–30, Pigeon Point to the U.S.–Mexico border, unless closed early.
salmon.bag: 2 salmon per person daily; one daily limit aboard. No coho or steelhead retention.
salmon.size: 20 in minimum total length during this fall season.
details: The fall fishery has a 20,000-Chinook harvest guideline and can close before Sep 30. Check CDFW immediately before the trip.
Do not fillet salmon aboard before landing ashore.
Gear rules depend on exact location and method; read the current official salmon regulations.
September season can close early on the harvest guideline. Coho may not be retained.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. U.S. waters south of Point Conception.
albacore.bag: 10 albacore south of Point Conception, in addition to the general 20-finfish daily aggregate. Special multi-day possession rules require separate review.
albacore.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The 25-albacore allowance north of Point Conception does not apply here.
Tuna schools and sea temperature fronts are mobile; a search area is not a catch site.
This package covers U.S. waters only; Mexican permits, limits and return rules are separate.

bluefin.name: Pacific bluefin tuna
bluefin.season: Year-round in the reviewed 2026 rules. Offshore U.S. waters off this part of California.
bluefin.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession on a day trip, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
bluefin.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The bluefin possession limit applies regardless of where fish were taken. This card does not cover Mexico or Atlantic bluefin.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. Check special rules before any multi-day trip.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.season: Not a promoted Southern California target. General scheduled recreational season opens November 7, 2026, subject to current restrictions; no regional grounds are qualified.
dungeness.bag: When open: 10 per person daily; 10 in possession on a private boat.
dungeness.size: 5¾ in shell width, measured across the body just in front of the side spines, excluding those spines. Carry a crab gauge.
details: The principal Dungeness fishery/range is north of Point Conception; this Southern package promotes California spiny lobster instead.
Crab traps, including loop traps/snares, are only authorized north of Point Arguello. Do not use the Central Coast trap/snare instructions here.
Any hoop or hand collection must satisfy current species, size, season, health, MPA and local access requirements. No local catch claim is made.

hoop.label: Hoop nets
hoop.note: Reference only: no local grounds qualified. Current hoop-net rules, season and local access must be checked.

hand.label: Hand collection
hand.note: Reference only: verify local species, season, access and method rules.

sheephead.name: California sheephead
sheephead.season: Boat rod-and-reel season March 1–December 31, 2026; closed January–February. Diver/shore exceptions are separate.
sheephead.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession; these count toward the general 20-finfish aggregate, not the RCG group.
details: Year-round diver/shore permission does not apply to rod fishing from the Parker.
The seasonal limit is separate from the rockfish/cabezon/greenling group; a mixed catch must still fit the general finfish limit.
If filleted aboard, minimum 6¾ in with all skin attached; keeping fish whole simplifies identification.

whitefish.name: Ocean whitefish
whitefish.season: Open all year and all depths in the reviewed 2026 rules, subject to place-specific closures.
whitefish.bag: 10 per person daily and in possession, within the general 20-finfish aggregate; separate from the 10-fish RCG group.
details: Ten RCG fish plus ten ocean whitefish already fill the general 20-finfish total; do not add lingcod or sheephead on top.
Rockfish/lingcod aboard impose their gear and closed-area possession rules even when targeting whitefish.
If filleted aboard, minimum 6½ in with all skin attached.

kelp-bass.name: Kelp bass / calico bass
kelp-bass.season: Open all year in the reviewed 2026 rules.
kelp-bass.bag: 5 total kelp, barred sand and spotted sand bass combined, with no more than 4 barred sand bass. Included in the general 20-finfish aggregate.
kelp-bass.size: 14 in minimum total length (or the regulation’s defined 10 in alternate length).
details: The five-fish limit is shared among all three bass species, not five of each. The current barred-sand-bass sublimit is four.
Identify the bass species. Bay/harbor access restrictions and MPAs apply independently.
If filleted aboard: at least 7½ in, with a one-inch-square skin patch.

white-seabass.name: White seabass
white-seabass.season: Open all year; reduced bag March 15–June 15 south of Point Conception.
white-seabass.bag: 3 per person daily/in possession, except 1 from March 15 through June 15; included in the general 20-finfish aggregate.
white-seabass.size: 28 in minimum total length. Use this agreed measurement; see the official full text for alternate-length rules.
details: Identify white seabass: giant/black seabass is protected and may not be retained in this U.S. fishery.
The reviewed CDFW summary and booklet disagree on alternate length; this card uses the 28-in total length that agrees in both sources.
If filleted aboard, minimum 19 in with a one-inch-square silver-skin patch.
An MPA exception for defined pelagic finfish does not automatically authorize white seabass or every fishing method.

yellowtail.size: 24 in minimum fork length, except up to 5 fish under 24 in fork length may be taken/possessed.

details: The undersized allowance is included in the ten-fish bag, not additional.

lobster.name: California spiny lobster
lobster.season: Next scheduled season: October 2, 2026 at 6 p.m. Pacific through March 17, 2027; check current notices before fishing.

windows.restriction: Not before 6 p.m. Pacific on October 2; verify opening notices, health, MPA and local method restrictions.

lobster.bag: 7 per person daily AND in possession, including retained lobsters at home. This is not a new seven-fish allowance on top of a retained limit.
lobster.size: 3¼ in minimum carapace length, from the rear edge of the eye socket to the rear edge of the body shell; carry and use a lobster gauge.
details: Lawful recreational methods are hands or legal hoop nets only. No traps, snares, rod-and-reel, spears or tickle sticks to take lobster.
All participants need a lobster report card, including children and people assisting with nets. Age 16+ generally need a fishing license and applicable ocean enhancement validation.
Record date, location and gear before starting; record catch when changing locations or finishing; report the card by April 30 even if no lobster was taken.
Measure immediately on retrieval; divers must measure underwater. Return undersized animals immediately. Keep lobsters whole and measurable until prepared for immediate consumption.

South of Point Arguello: maximum five hoop nets for one hoop operator; maximum ten per vessel with two or more operators. Follow construction/marking rules and raise/inspect every deployed hoop at least every two hours.
Hoop nets may not be deployed/used south of Point Arguello during the 24 hours before the lobster opener.
Off Anacapa, nets and traps are prohibited in water shallower than 20 ft; West Anacapa has a separate January–October access closure. All mapped MPAs are excluded from this app’s target areas.
The 2027 part of the scheduled season is context only; this reviewed registry expires December 31, 2026 and must be renewed.

hoop.label: Hoop nets
hoop.note: Use legal hoop nets with the required surface buoy/GO ID, counts, attendance and retrieval checks. No deployment during the 24 hours before the opener. Verify site and current notices.

hand.label: Hand collection
hand.note: Divers collect by hand only, with report card and gauge; measure underwater. Check diving conditions and access separately. No tools may help capture a lobster.

common_notes: Limits are per angler on a day trip. Unless a species has an express exception, the general limit is 20 finfish total with no more than ten of one species and any lower species/group limit still applies.

RCG, lingcod, sheephead, ocean whitefish, halibut, bass, yellowtail, bonito, barracuda, white seabass, yellowfin and dorado all count toward that general 20. Bluefin and the regional albacore allowance are express additional-limit exceptions.

A California fishing license is normally required at age 16+. Applicable ocean enhancement validation, species report cards, landing-net and identification requirements also apply; lobster report cards are required regardless of age.

With rockfish, lingcod or other covered groundfish aboard, their one-line/two-hook and closed-area possession restrictions continue when switching targets. Do not apply unlimited general lines to a mixed groundfish trip.

For finfish, have a landing net at least 18 in in diameter available. Within 1,000 yd of the mainland/island shoreline south of Pigeon Point, metallic/wire leaders and hooks wider than 1½ in inside are prohibited.

Seasonal groundfish access follows the legal 50-fathom RCA coordinate line, not a 300-ft reading on the sounder. Groundfish Exclusion Areas and species-specific possession restrictions remain in effect.

SkipperCast withholds target geometries in all mapped MPAs, including some conservation areas with lawful method/species exceptions. This conservative display policy is not a statement that every MPA is legally no-take. State/federal MPA and special-closure boundaries must all be checked.

Anacapa has additional net/trap and seasonal pelican-area restrictions. Island military operations, harbor/anchorage restrictions and the international maritime boundary require separate access checks.
The selected bottom-depth limit remains in force. A center sounding or broad species depth range does not qualify an entire search area.
These are reviewed summaries, not automatic legal clearance. Source changes, missing checks, health notices and exact position/method can change access; use the linked official rules before fishing.
